title: Your car is selling where you drive.
excerpt: A Northeastern/Consumer Reports study found nearly all 19 car brands share driver data — GPS per trip, braking, in-cabin camera. The FTC found GM sold geolocation from millions of cars. The thing you drive is a data broker on wheels.
content_html:
Ψ AURAVISION · FIELD BRIEF PRIVACY INTELLIGENCE

Your car is selling your every move.

A Northeastern University and Consumer Reports study of 21 vehicles across 19 brands found that nearly every automaker sends driver data to outside companies — precise GPS for every trip, braking and acceleration, even in-cabin camera footage. In 2026 the FTC found GM sold geolocation from millions of cars without proper consent.

19 brands

nearly all shared driver data

millions

of cars' geolocation sold (GM/FTC)

every trip

precise GPS collected

What happened

Northeastern and Consumer Reports tested 21 vehicles from 19 brands; nearly all transmitted driver data to third parties, including some of the world's largest ad companies. Collected data spans precise GPS per trip, speed/braking/acceleration, seatbelt use, infotainment usage, seat-sensor biometrics, and in-cabin camera footage. In 2026 the FTC's order against GM/OnStar found it collected and sold precise geolocation and driving behavior from millions of vehicles without adequate consent — data that flows on to banks, insurers, and lenders.

Why it matters

Your car knows where you sleep, work, worship, and shop — and it's selling that map. You can't opt a modern car out of the internet; the data pipe is wired in at the factory, and the buyer might be your insurer.

It knows everywhere you go

Precise GPS for every trip, routed to data brokers.

Even the cabin camera

In-car footage and seat-sensor biometrics are in scope.

Sold to your insurer

Driving data becomes your risk profile — and your rate.

The only device that can't sell your life is one that was never listening out.

The principle

The rule people who run infrastructure live by: never connect the things you care about to the internet. If a product can phone home, assume it does — and assume someone's buying.

Aura's answer

Intelligence that doesn't log your life.

Aura runs entirely on-device — no telemetry pipe, no broker feed, no profile built from your day. It hears only you, and nothing it hears leaves the room. The product isn't the data; the product is the device. Nothing leaves the room.
